Debut

/deb-YOO/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Debut is first appearance in a role or capacity.

The young violinist made her debut with the city orchestra last spring.

Worked Example

Backstage, a seventeen-year-old violinist adjusts her bow with shaking hands. In a few minutes she will walk onto a professional concert stage and play for a paying audience for the very first time in her life.

This is her first-ever public appearance as a performer, and that formal first showing is exactly what a debut is. Debut is more precise than 'start' or 'beginning' because it names a first presentation before the public, not just the first step of any process.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

premiere: the first public showing of something

introduction: the act of presenting something new

launch: the official start or unveiling

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

finale: the closing performance or final part

farewell: a final appearance before departing

Where it sits · how public and grand the occasion is — tryout → introduction → debut → premiere

tryout vs. debut: A tryout is smaller-scale than a debut — a tryout is a private test of your skills, while a debut is your official first appearance before the public.

introduction vs. debut: An introduction is weaker than a debut; an introduction simply presents someone new, but a debut marks a performer's formal first appearance in a role.

premiere vs. debut: A premiere is grander than a debut — a debut can be any first public appearance, while a premiere is the celebrated, red-carpet first showing of a major work.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — debut

root — debut: a first stroke toward a goal; a beginning (French (débuter, from but 'goal, target'))

Put it together

Put it together: From French débuter, 'to make the first stroke toward the target (but)': a debut is your opening move — a first appearance in a role or before the public.

Use the root in a new word: debutante

Use the root in a new word: debutante: The debutante was formally introduced to society at the spring ball.

Word Building

Word Choice

Debut most naturally pairs with the verb 'make' (make her debut) and is often narrowed by a field word placed just before it — a film debut, a stage debut, a debut album — to specify exactly what kind of first appearance is meant.
